name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

findings.summary: LIME, Cable & Wireless's Caribbean arm, contracted Ericsson to modernise its mobile networks in 12 territories including Saint Vincent, with a new core network and multi-standard radio base stations plus design, rollout and services.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) as equipment vendor, so pole third. Two opened S2 reports likely both relay one Ericsson/LIME announcement, so not treated as independent. Tier 3 (contract); SVG-specific rollout not confirmed. Pre-2020; current Flow SVG vendor not reconfirmed.

findings.summary: A 2006 report on Digicel's Turks and Caicos network said Ericsson had been Digicel's preferred network vendor in several markets, naming Saint Vincent and the Grenadines among them.
findings.analyst_inference: Background mention only, not a dedicated SVG award; tier 5 assumes the Digicel GSM network was operational on Ericsson kit. Pre-2020; Digicel's 2018 LTE launch (BNamericas, opened) named no vendor, so current vendor unknown.

findings.controller: Not stated (cable supplier unnamed; laid by vessel CS Intrepid)
findings.local_actor: Government of St. Vincent and the Grenadines; Digicel (SVG) Ltd (public-private partnership)
findings.summary: A World Bank-funded CARCIP subsea fibre cable, delivered as a government–Digicel partnership, linked mainland St Vincent with Bequia, Mustique, Canouan, Union Island, Carriacou and Grenada; subsea laying was completed May 2019, terrestrial network due later.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance, St. Vincent and the Grenadines

findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: equipment vendor (sets pole for cables) not named and asset owner/operator under the PPP unclear. World Bank financier does not set pole. Tier 4: subsea laying done, network completion not confirmed. Single opened S1 (NBC echoes it, S4), so medium.

findings.local_actor: Royal St. Vincent and the Grenadines Police Force; Information Technology Services Division
findings.summary: Taiwan-funded police CCTV ('Intelligent Video Analytics') programme: 172 cameras in Phase 1 (2021); Phase 2, launched March 2023 and including licence-plate recognition cameras, closed August 2025 with nearly 300 cameras across 20+ sites.

sources.publisher: Ministry of National Security, St. Vincent and the Grenadines

findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no source names the camera or analytics vendor, which would set the pole; police operate it domestically and Taiwan is donor, not documented controller. Not a PRC safe-city deployment. Corroborated by S1 ministry release plus independent S3 reporting; 2025 report drew on a Taiwanese Embassy release. Camera totals across phases may overlap.
